title: Pilgrimage
examples: Why do people go on pilgrimage?

figure.label: Great pilgrimage places of the world

explain.say: A pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place, made for faith rather than for a holiday. Here are some of the world's great pilgrimage places, from Mecca to Jerusalem, Prayagraj, Bodh Gaya and Amritsar.

The Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca, the fifth Pillar of Islam. Every adult Muslim who is healthy and can afford it should go once in their life, in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah. Pilgrims dress simply, circle the Kaaba, and pray together at Arafat.

items: Put on ihram, simple white clothing
Pray at the plain of Arafat
Eid al-Adha, the festival of sacrifice

draw.text: Around two million Muslims make the Hajj in a typical recent year.

explain.say: The Kumbh Mela is a Hindu festival of bathing in sacred rivers, held in turn at four places. At Prayagraj, where the Ganges and Yamuna rivers meet, it is among the largest gatherings of people on Earth.

draw.label: Kumbh Mela at Prayagraj; Varanasi on the Ganges

draw.text: Officials counted hundreds of millions of visits at the 2025 Maha Kumbh at Prayagraj.

explain.say: Jerusalem is a pilgrimage city for three faiths. Jews pray at the Western Wall, Christians visit the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, and Muslims pray at the Al-Aqsa Mosque, the third holiest site in Islam.

items: Jewish | The Western Wall, last wall of the Temple Mount
Christian | Church of the Holy Sepulchre
Muslim | Al-Aqsa Mosque and the Dome of the Rock

explain.say: Buddhists visit the four places of the Buddha's life: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar. Sikhs love to visit the Golden Temple in Amritsar, though Sikh teaching says the truest pilgrimage is remembering God within.

draw.label: The Buddha's four places, and the Golden Temple

explain.say: Why make such a journey? Pilgrims speak of feeling closer to God or the sacred, of fulfilling a duty, seeking forgiveness or healing, giving thanks, and coming home changed.

faq.a: The Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca in Saudi Arabia, the fifth Pillar of Islam. Every adult Muslim who is physically and financially able should make it once in their life. It takes place over several days in the Islamic month of Dhu al-Hijjah, with rituals that remember the Prophet Abraham and his family.
asks: what is the pilgrimage to Mecca
what do Muslims do in Mecca

faq.q: Why do people go on pilgrimage?
faq.a: People go on pilgrimage to feel closer to God or the sacred, to follow in the footsteps of their faith's founders, to fulfil a religious duty, to pray for healing or forgiveness, or to give thanks. Many say the journey itself, shared with others, changes them.
asks: what is the point of a pilgrimage

faq.a: The Kumbh Mela is a Hindu festival in which pilgrims bathe in sacred rivers, which many believe washes away sins. It rotates between Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik, and at Prayagraj, where the Ganges and Yamuna meet, it is among the largest gatherings of people on Earth.
asks: what happens at the Kumbh Mela

faq.q: What do pilgrims do on the Hajj?
faq.a: Pilgrims put on ihram, simple white clothing that makes everyone equal, circle the Kaaba seven times, walk seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa, stand in prayer on the plain of Arafat, and throw pebbles at pillars at Mina. The Hajj ends with Eid al-Adha.
asks: what are the steps of Hajj
why do pilgrims wear white on Hajj

faq.a: The Kaaba is the cube-shaped building at the centre of the Great Mosque in Mecca, covered in a black cloth. Muslims believe it was built by Abraham and his son Ishmael as a house for the worship of one God. Muslims face it when they pray, but they worship God alone, not the building.
asks: what is the black cube in Mecca

faq.a: The Umrah is a shorter pilgrimage to Mecca that Muslims can make at any time of year. It is recommended but not compulsory, while the Hajj takes place only in its set days and is a duty for those able.

faq.q: Why is Jerusalem a place of pilgrimage?
faq.a: Jerusalem is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims. Jews pray at the Western Wall, near the site of the ancient Temple; Christians visit places linked to Jesus's death and resurrection; and Muslims pray at the Al-Aqsa Mosque, linked to the Prophet's Night Journey.

faq.q: Where do Buddhists go on pilgrimage?
faq.a: Many Buddhists visit four places linked to the Buddha's life: Lumbini where he was born, Bodh Gaya where he became enlightened under the Bodhi tree, Sarnath where he first taught, and Kushinagar where he died.

Sikh teaching says pilgrimage is not required, because God is found by remembering God and living well every day. Even so, many Sikhs love to visit the Golden Temple in Amritsar and other gurdwaras linked to the Gurus' lives.

faq.q: Where do Christians go on pilgrimage?
faq.a: Christians visit the Holy Land, where Jesus lived, and places such as Rome and the Vatican, Lourdes in France, and Santiago de Compostela in Spain, where many walk the long route called the Camino.
asks: why do Catholics go to Lourdes

faq.q: Why is Varanasi holy to Hindus?
faq.a: Varanasi, on the banks of the Ganges, is one of the holiest cities in Hinduism and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Pilgrims bathe in the river at the ghats, the stone steps, and many Hindus hope to be cremated there.
asks: why do Hindus bathe in the Ganges

faq.q: How many people go on the Hajj?
faq.a: In recent years about two million Muslims have made the Hajj, and in some years more. Saudi Arabia sets limits for each country so the holy sites are not overcrowded.
asks: how many pilgrims go to Mecca

faq.a: Mount Kailash in Tibet is sacred to Hindus, who see it as the home of Shiva, and to Buddhists, Jains and followers of Bon. Pilgrims walk all the way around it, a route of about 52 kilometres, but by custom no one climbs it.
No. Only Muslims may enter the holy city of Mecca, and Saudi Arabia enforces this. Many other pilgrimage sites, such as the Golden Temple, Bodh Gaya and Varanasi, welcome visitors of every faith.
asks: are non Muslims allowed in Mecca

facts: The Hajj is the fifth Pillar of Islam and takes place in the Islamic month of Dhu al-Hijjah.
The Kumbh Mela rotates between Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik, and is among the largest gatherings on Earth.
The four main Buddhist pilgrimage places are Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Kushinagar.
The Western Wall in Jerusalem is the holiest place where Jews can pray today.
The langar at the Golden Temple in Amritsar serves free meals to tens of thousands of people every day.

quiz.say: Recall. The Hajj is which Pillar of Islam?
quiz.show: The Hajj is which Pillar of Islam?
quiz.why: The five Pillars are the declaration of faith, prayer, charity, fasting in Ramadan, and the Hajj, the fifth.

wrong.0: The first Pillar is the Shahada, the declaration of faith.
wrong.1: The third Pillar is zakat, giving to those in need.

quiz.say: Apply. Millions of pilgrims gather where two great rivers meet, to bathe and pray. Which pilgrimage is this?
quiz.show: Bathing where the Ganges and Yamuna meet: which pilgrimage?
quiz.why: At Prayagraj, the Kumbh Mela brings Hindu pilgrims to bathe where the Ganges and Yamuna meet.

wrong.0: The Hajj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, in the desert of Arabia.
wrong.2: The Camino is a Christian walking route to Santiago de Compostela in Spain.
wrong.3: Bodh Gaya is where the Buddha became enlightened, under the Bodhi tree.

quiz.say: Think. Pilgrims on the Hajj all wear the same simple white clothing. What idea does that express?
quiz.show: Why do Hajj pilgrims dress alike in simple white?

options.show: White is cooler in the heat, nothing more
options.say: White is cooler in the heat, nothing more

quiz.why: Ihram removes signs of wealth and rank, so rich and poor stand together as equals before God.

wrong.1: White may be cooler, but the clothing has a deeper religious meaning of equality and purity.
wrong.2: It does the opposite: everyone looks the same, so wealth is hidden.
